lessons.title: Starting Key Stage 3: goals, the rubric and the revision log
lessons.bigQuestion: A footballer practises the same basics every day. What are the 'basics' of good recitation, and why practise them again in Year 7?
objectives: To understand how recitation is assessed in Key Stage 3 and to set a personal hifdh and tajweed goal for the year
successCriteria: All: explain the five rubric rows in your own words
Most: set a hifdh target and a tajweed target from your placement
Some: plan a weekly revision cycle for Juz' 'Amma

hook.text: A footballer practises the same basics every day. What are the 'basics' of good recitation, and why practise them again in Year 7?
hook.a: Correct makharij, sifat and rules: in Key Stage 3 we move from knowing rules to using them without thinking.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4). The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it' (Bukhari).

starter.q: How many surahs are in Juz' 'Amma (78 to 114)?

teach.heading: The Key Stage 3 rubric
teach.note: Bismillah. Walk through each row with one example. It is a tool for growth, not for comparing pupils.

bullets: Hifdh target: where you start
Tajweed target: one rule to fix
Year 7 aim: complete Juz' 'Amma
teach.note: Each pupil has their induction-week placement in the portal. Year 7 minimum: 'Abasa, An-Nazi'at and An-Naba' (80 to 78), completing Juz' 'Amma.

teach.heading: The revision log
bullets: Sabaq: new ayat (daily)
Sabqi: last week's ayat
Manzil: older surahs on a rota
Log it daily in the portal
teach.note: Show the portal revision log. 10 to 15 minutes a day. A parent initials it weekly.

teach.note: Explain the routine used every week.

teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

options: older surahs revised on a rota
check.why: Sabaq is new ayat; sabqi is recent; manzil is the older memorised portion revised on a rota.

practice.q: Score this example against the rubric: a pupil recites Al-Fatihah fluently but says ٱلْحَمْدُ with a 'h' instead of ح.
practice.a: Hifdh 4; makharij 2 (ح said as ه); rules 4; fluency 4; target: ح from the middle of the throat.
practice.model: I do: hifdh: no prompts, 4. Makharij: ح became ه, which changes the letter, so 2. Rules and fluency fine, 4. One target: say ح from the middle of the throat.

practice.q: Year 7 hifdh minimum completes ...
practice.a: Juz' 'Amma

independent.q: In the portal response box, write your hifdh target, one tajweed target and your weekly revision plan (sabaq, sabqi, manzil). Today's rota group recites Al-Fatihah and one short surah.
independent.a: A realistic plan: e.g. sabaq 'Abasa 1 to 8; sabqi last week's ayat; manzil 114 to 100 over the week.
independent.model: The teacher models a plan: 'Sabaq: 'Abasa 1 to 8 this week. Sabqi: revise Monday's ayat each day. Manzil: two short surahs a day from 114 down.'

independent.q: Extend: choose the time of day you will revise and why.
independent.a: For example: after Fajr, when the mind is fresh.

independent.q: Stretch: explain why revising old surahs matters as much as learning new ones.
independent.a: Memorised Qur'an escapes without revision (Bukhari and Muslim: it escapes faster than camels from their hobbles).

exit.q: New ayat for today are called ...
exit.a: sabaq

exit.q: Back to our ponder: A footballer practises the same basics every day. What are the 'basics' of good recitation, and why practise them again in Year 7?
exit.a: Correct makharij, sifat and rules: in Key Stage 3 we move from knowing rules to using them without thinking.

lessons.title: Makharij 1: the jawf and the throat
lessons.bigQuestion: عَلِيم means 'all-knowing'; أَلِيم means 'painful'. One letter changes. What does that tell you about makharij?
objectives: To understand where the madd letters and the six throat letters are produced and to pronounce them precisely

hook.text: عَلِيم means 'all-knowing'; أَلِيم means 'painful'. One letter changes. What does that tell you about makharij?

teach.note: Read each; pupils echo with mics in turn.

check.q: Which pair comes from the middle of the throat?

practice.q: Read «وَهُوَ يَخْشَىٰ» (80:9) and name the makhraj of ه and خ.
practice.a: ه: deepest part of the throat; خ: part nearest the mouth.
practice.model: I do: وَ: lips. هُ: deepest part of the throat, near the chest. وَ: lips. يَ: middle of the tongue. خْ: upper throat, near the mouth, heavy. شَىٰ: middle of the tongue, then the alif from the jawf.

practice.q: Madd letters come from ...
practice.a: the jawf

independent.q: Throat-letter audit (pupil PDF): circle and label every throat letter in 'Abasa 80:1 to 10. Today's rota group recites 80:1 to 8 to the teacher.
independent.model: The teacher labels the first: ع in عَبَسَ, middle of the throat.

independent.q: Extend: write a pair of words where ع and ء change the meaning.
independent.a: عَلِيم (all-knowing) and أَلِيم (painful).

independent.q: Stretch: why are throat letters the izhar letters for noon sakinah?
independent.a: They are far from the tongue tip where noon is made, so the noon stays clear.

exit.q: خ is made ...
exit.a: in the throat, nearest the mouth
options: in the throat, nearest the mouth

exit.q: Back to our ponder: عَلِيم means 'all-knowing'; أَلِيم means 'painful'. One letter changes. What does that tell you about makharij?
exit.a: A letter from the wrong place can change the meaning completely, so makharij matter.

lessons.title: Makharij 2: the tongue
lessons.bigQuestion: The tongue makes 18 of the 28 letters. Why might Allah have given such a small muscle so much work?
objectives: To understand the main exit points of the tongue and pronounce the tongue letters precisely in recitation
successCriteria: All: name which part of the tongue makes ق ك, ج ش ي and ض
Most: separate ظ ذ ث from ص ز س

lessons.crossCurricular: Science: muscles and the human body

keywords.def: the exit point of a letter (plural makharij, مخارج)

hook.text: The tongue makes 18 of the 28 letters. Why might Allah have given such a small muscle so much work?
hook.a: It is a sign of Allah's design; we thank Him by using the tongue for good speech and His words.

teach.note: Bismillah. Pupils say each with a fathah. ض is the hardest: the side of the tongue presses the upper back teeth.

teach.note: Raa is one touch, not a roll.

teach.note: Read each word; pupils echo.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: Which letter is made with the side of the tongue?
check.why: ض alone is from the side. ظ is the tip on the edge of the top teeth; ط the tip on the roots.

practice.q: Read «أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنفَعَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰٓ» (80:4) and name the makhraj of each ذ and ك.
practice.a: ذ: tip on the edge of the top teeth; ك: back of the tongue (a little forward of ق).
practice.model: I do: يَذَّ: tongue tip peeps to the edge of the top teeth, doubled. كَّ: back of tongue, doubled. ٱلذِّكْرَىٰٓ: same ذ, then ك, then stretch.

practice.q: Whistling letters?
practice.a: ص ز س

independent.q: Makharij audit (pupil PDF): for 80:9 to 16, label each tongue letter with its point. Today's rota group recites 80:1 to 8.
independent.a: e.g. ش يَخْشَىٰ middle; ل تَلَهَّىٰ edge to tip; ك كَلَّآ back; ذ تَذْكِرَةٌ tip and top teeth edge; ص صُحُفٍ whistle; ط مُّطَهَّرَةٍ tip and roots; ر بَرَرَةٍ tip with gum.
independent.model: The teacher labels the first: ش in يَخْشَىٰ, middle of the tongue.

independent.q: Extend: say three pairs that are often confused and the difference.
independent.a: ث/س: peeps out vs whistle; ذ/ز; ظ/ض: tip vs side.

independent.q: Stretch: why is Arabic called 'the language of the daad'?
independent.a: ض is a sound few other languages have, so Arabic is named after it.

exit.q: ث is made ...
exit.a: with the tongue tip on the edge of the top teeth
options: with the tongue tip on the edge of the top teeth
with the side of the tongue

exit.q: Back to our ponder: The tongue makes 18 of the 28 letters. Why might Allah have given such a small muscle so much work?
exit.a: It is a sign of Allah's design; we thank Him by using the tongue for good speech and His words.

independent.q: Extend: which letters have ghunnah in their nature?

independent.q: Stretch: why is 17 points but 29 letters?
independent.a: Several letters share a point and differ by their sifat (e.g. ط د ت).

exit.q: Which lip letter is a 'stop'?
exit.a: ب

hook.text: Raa and laam are light letters, yet sometimes we say them heavy. How can one letter be both?
hook.a: They are not isti'la letters, so their weight depends on the vowels around them.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And to Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them' (Al-A'raf 7:180). The laam in His Name is said with care.

starter.a: و or ي sakin after fathah
options: و or ي sakin after fathah

starter.q: Recite 'Abasa 80:28 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: Raa with a vowel
teach.note: Bismillah. Look at the raa's own vowel first.

teach.heading: Raa with sukoon: look before it
bullets: After fathah or dammah: heavy (تَرْهَقُهَا)
After an original kasrah: light (فِرْعَوْنَ)
But heavy if an isti'la letter follows in the word (مِرْصَادًا)
After hamzat al-wasl: heavy (ٱرْجِعِىٓ)
teach.note: تَرْهَقُهَا is 80:41. فِرْعَوْنَ is 79:17; مِرْصَادًا is 78:21; ٱرْجِعِىٓ is 89:28: all in Juz' 'Amma.

teach.heading: The laam in the Name Allah
bullets: After fathah or dammah: heavy (هُوَ ٱللَّهُ)
After kasrah: light (بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ)
Every other laam is light
teach.note: Revise from Year 5.

practice.q: Decide heavy or light: «فَأَقْبَرَهُۥ» (80:21), «ٱمْرِئٍۢ» (80:37), «فِرْعَوْنَ» (79:17).
practice.a: فَأَقْبَرَهُۥ heavy (fathah); ٱمْرِئٍ light (kasrah); فِرْعَوْنَ light (sukoon after kasrah, no isti'la after).
practice.model: I do: فَأَقْبَرَهُۥ: the raa has fathah, heavy. ٱمْرِئٍ: the raa has kasrah, light. فِرْعَوْنَ: raa sakinah, before it ف with kasrah, and no isti'la letter after it in the word, so light.

practice.q: «بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ»: the laam is ...
practice.a: light

independent.q: Raa audit (pupil PDF): mark every raa in 'Abasa 80:34 to 42 H or L with a reason. Today's rota group recites 80:25 to 33.
independent.a: ٱلْمَرْءُ H (sukoon after fathah); ٱمْرِئٍ L (kasrah); مُّسْفِرَةٌ H (fathah); مُّسْتَبْشِرَةٌ H (fathah); غَبَرَةٌ H; تَرْهَقُهَا H; قَتَرَةٌ H; ٱلْكَفَرَةُ H; ٱلْفَجَرَةُ H.
independent.model: The teacher marks the first: ٱلْمَرْءُ (80:34): raa sakinah after fathah, heavy.

independent.q: Extend: find the Name Allah in Al-Ikhlas and say heavy or light.
independent.a: Heavy both times (112:1 after fathah; 112:2 starting).

independent.q: Stretch: why is the raa in مِرْصَادًا heavy, though a kasrah comes before?
independent.a: An isti'la letter (ص) follows the raa in the same word.

exit.q: Raa with kasrah is ...
exit.a: light

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Raa and laam are light letters, yet sometimes we say them heavy. How can one letter be both?
exit.a: They are not isti'la letters, so their weight depends on the vowels around them.

lessons.title: Madd 1: the two families

objectives: To understand how every madd belongs to one of two families, natural or caused, and how the cause sets its length
successCriteria: All: say whether a madd is natural (asli) or caused (far'i)
Most: name the cause: a hamza or a sukoon
Some: sort ten madds from An-Nazi'at and justify the counts

keywords.def: the natural madd: 2 counts, no cause
a longer madd caused by a hamza or a sukoon
the cause of a longer madd: hamza or sukoon

hook.text: Why might Allah's Book be recited with exact lengths, when everyday speech is not so careful?
hook.a: It is Allah's word, recited exactly as the Prophet ﷺ taught it; exact lengths keep it unchanged.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4). Madd is a core part of tarteel.

teach.heading: Two families
bullets: Asli (natural): no cause, 2 counts
Far'i (caused): a hamza or a sukoon follows
The cause makes it longer
teach.note: Bismillah. Welcome back. Founding-year order (Year 7 pack): An-Nazi'at 79:1 to 46 is the new hifdh this half term, with madd and stopping; An-Naba' follows.

teach.heading: The family table
teach.note: Read each row; every example is from An-Nazi'at.

teach.heading: Find the cause
teach.note: Use this every time.
cycle: Find the madd letter
Look after it: hamza? sukoon? nothing?
Same word or next word?
Choose the family and counts
Recite with even counts

teach.heading: Common mistake
teach.note: Lengths must be steady and consistent.

misconception.wrong: Guessing a length by feel, so the same madd changes each time
misconception.right: Count every madd on the fingers until the length is automatic

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: Alif then hamza in the same word: muttasil, 4 or 5.

practice.q: Label each madd in «فَإِذَا جَآءَتِ ٱلطَّآمَّةُ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ» (79:34).
practice.a: فَإِذَا: natural (2); جَآءَتِ: muttasil (4 or 5); ٱلطَّآمَّةُ: lazim (6); ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ: natural (2), even at the stop, because the word ends on the madd letter.
practice.model: I do: إِذَا: alif, no cause: natural. جَآءَتِ: hamza in the word: muttasil. ٱلطَّآمَّةُ: alif then a shaddah: lazim, six. ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ ends on the alif itself, so nothing comes after it: natural, two.

practice.q: A madd with no cause is ...
practice.a: asli (natural)

independent.q: Sort (pupil PDF): put ten madds from 79:1 to 20 into natural, muttasil or munfasil, with the counts. Today's rota group recites 'Abasa to the teacher.
independent.a: For example: ٱلنَّٰزِعَٰتِ natural; مُوسَىٰٓ munfasil when joined to إِذْ (79:16), natural at a stop; إِلَىٰٓ أَن munfasil; ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ natural.
independent.model: The teacher sorts the first two aloud.

independent.q: Extend: explain why 'arid lis-sukun only happens when stopping.
independent.a: The sukoon is not fixed: it appears only because we stop on the word.

independent.q: Stretch: give one madd of each family from Al-Fatihah.
independent.a: Natural: مَٰلِكِ; 'arid: ٱلرَّحِيمِ at the stop; lazim: ٱلضَّآلِّينَ.

exit.q: Madd lazim is always ...
exit.a: 6 counts

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Why might Allah's Book be recited with exact lengths, when everyday speech is not so careful?
exit.a: It is Allah's word, recited exactly as the Prophet ﷺ taught it; exact lengths keep it unchanged.

hook.text: Some surahs begin with separate letters like «الٓمٓ». Why do you think we read them by their names, not their sounds?

What we see
Example

practice.q: Harfi means the madd is in ...

exit.q: Madd lazim is held for ...
exit.a: 6 counts

lessons.bigQuestion: A poor, blind man comes to ask about Islam while you are busy with important people. What would you do, and why?

lessons.smsc: Moral: every person deserves respect; sincerity matters more than status

hook.text: A poor, blind man comes to ask about Islam while you are busy with important people. What would you do, and why?
hook.a: Allah taught that the sincere seeker deserves our full attention: worth is in the heart, not status (80:1 to 10).

islamicLink.text: These ayat were revealed about 'Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, a blind Companion who came to the Prophet ﷺ to learn while he was speaking to leaders of Quraysh (Tirmidhi). Allah teaches that the one who comes seeking and fearing Allah must be welcomed (Abasa 80:8 to 10).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: The Prophet frowned and turned away
Because there came to him the blind man, [interrupting].
But what would make you perceive, [O Muhammad], that perhaps he might be purified
Or be reminded and the remembrance would benefit him?
As for he who thinks himself without need,
And not upon you [is any blame] if he will not be purified.
But as for he who came to you striving [for knowledge]

lessons.title: Muraja'ah: the Juz' 'Amma rota and 'Abasa 1 to 16
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do people forget surahs they once knew perfectly? What would stop that happening to you?
objectives: To understand how to revise memorised surahs efficiently and to recite 'Abasa 80:1 to 16 with correct makharij
successCriteria: All: recite 'Abasa 80:1 to 16 with no more than two prompts
Most: revise two manzil surahs with a partner using the rubric
Some: identify your 'weak links' (ayat you often swap) and fix them
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: keeping a promise to the Qur'an through steady revision

keywords.def: revision of what is already memorised
the older memorised portion, revised on a rota
a place where you often pause or swap ayat

hook.text: Why do people forget surahs they once knew perfectly? What would stop that happening to you?
hook.a: Lack of revision. A steady rota (sabaq, sabqi, manzil) keeps everything fresh.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Keep refreshing your knowledge of the Qur'an, for by Him in whose hand is my soul, it escapes faster than camels from their hobbles' (Bukhari and Muslim).

starter.q: Recite 'Abasa 80:12 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: The rota this week
teach.note: Bismillah. Show each group's manzil for the week. Groups are set by the placement.

teach.heading: Weak links
bullets: Where do you pause or swap ayat?
Mark them in pencil
Recite the two ayat around it 5 times
teach.note: Example: 80:6 and 80:10 both begin فَأَنتَ. Pupils often jump. Practise 80:5 to 6 and 80:9 to 10 together.

teach.heading: Partner check with the rubric
bullets: Partner holds the mushaf
Mark prompts and rule mistakes
Give one kind target
teach.note: Breakout pairs, 4 minutes each way.

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: 80:1 to 16 one ayah at a time, with attention to makharij.
cycle: Teacher recites one ayah
Pupils listen, eyes on the mushaf
Three pupils repeat in turn
Teacher corrects one makhraj
Whole class repeats softly

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: Both begin فَأَنتَ (80:6 تَصَدَّىٰ; 80:10 تَلَهَّىٰ): a classic weak link.

practice.q: Fix the weak link: recite 80:5 to 6 and 80:9 to 10 and say what comes after each فَأَنتَ.
practice.a: 80:6 فَأَنتَ لَهُۥ تَصَدَّىٰ; 80:10 فَأَنتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّىٰ.
practice.model: I do: 'the one who thinks himself without need (80:5): you give him attention, فَأَنتَ لَهُۥ تَصَدَّىٰ'. 'The one who fears (80:9): from him you are distracted, فَأَنتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّىٰ'. The meaning tells me which comes where.

practice.q: Best time to fix a weak link?
practice.a: Straight away, five times

independent.q: Breakout pairs: recite your manzil surahs for today to a partner who marks the rubric on the pupil PDF. Today's rota group recites 80:1 to 16 to the teacher.
independent.a: Rubric scores and one target for each partner; the teacher records the rota group's scores.
independent.model: The teacher and a volunteer model one round: recite, mark, one kind target.

independent.q: Extend: list your three weakest links in Juz' 'Amma.
Stretch: explain how the meaning helps fix a weak link, with an example.
independent.a: In 80:6 the rich man gets attention; in 80:10 the sincere seeker is neglected: meaning orders the words.

exit.a: recent ayat (last week)

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Why do people forget surahs they once knew perfectly? What would stop that happening to you?
exit.a: Lack of revision. A steady rota (sabaq, sabqi, manzil) keeps everything fresh.

[From] the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful. They possess not from Him [authority for] speech.
The Day that the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak except for one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is correct.
That is the True Day; so he who wills may take to his Lord a [way of] return.
Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment on the Day when a man will observe what his hands have put forth and the disbeliever will say, "Oh, I wish that I were dust!"
